Bivariate Data and Correlation: Bivariate data
Data recording two variables for each individual
Scatterplot
A plot of ordered pairs showing the relationship between two variables
Explanatory variable
The variable plotted on the horizontal axis as the predictor
Response variable
The variable plotted on the vertical axis as the outcome
Positive association
Larger values of one variable accompanying larger values of the other
Negative association
Larger values of one variable accompanying smaller values of the other
Correlation coefficient
A value between negative one and one measuring linear strength
Perfect correlation
A correlation of exactly one or negative one, all points on a line
No linear correlation
A correlation near zero, indicating no straight-line pattern
Correlation is not causation
An association may be caused by a third variable
Lurking variable
An unmeasured variable influencing both variables studied
Effect of outliers on r
A single extreme point can dramatically change the correlation
Linear Regression: Regression line
The straight line that best summarises a linear relationship
Least-squares criterion
Minimising the total of squared vertical distances to the line
Slope of a regression line
The predicted change in y for each one-unit rise in x
y-intercept of a regression line
The predicted y value when x equals zero
Prediction
Using the regression equation to estimate an unobserved y
Residual
The difference between an observed value and its prediction
Residual plot
A plot of residuals used to judge whether a line fits
Random residual pattern
Evidence that a linear model is appropriate
Curved residual pattern
Evidence that a linear model is inappropriate
Coefficient of determination
The fraction of variation in y explained by x
Interpolation versus extrapolation
Predicting within versus beyond the observed x range
Influential observation
A point whose removal substantially changes the line

Confidence Intervals: Confidence interval
A range of plausible values for an unknown parameter
Point estimate
A single value used to estimate a parameter
Margin of error
The amount added and subtracted around a point estimate
Confidence level
The percentage of such intervals that would capture the parameter
Critical value
The multiplier corresponding to a chosen confidence level
Interval for a proportion
An interval built around a sample proportion
Interval for a mean
An interval built around a sample mean using t values
Interpretation of a confidence interval
Confidence describes the method, not one specific interval
Wider versus narrower intervals
Higher confidence widens and larger samples narrow the interval
Choosing sample size
Solving for n to meet a target margin of error

Hypothesis Testing: Hypothesis test
A procedure evaluating evidence against a claim
Null hypothesis
The default claim of no effect or no difference
Alternative hypothesis
The claim the researcher hopes to support
One-sided test
A test looking for a difference in only one direction
Two-sided test
A test looking for a difference in either direction
Test statistic
A standardised measure of the distance from the null value
P-value
The probability of data this extreme when the null is true
Significance level
The cutoff, often 0.05, for declaring results significant
Rejecting the null hypothesis
Concluding the evidence is strong enough against the default claim
Failing to reject the null
Concluding the evidence is insufficient, not that the null is true
Type I error
Rejecting a null hypothesis that is actually true
Type II error
Failing to reject a null hypothesis that is actually false
Statistical significance
A result unlikely to be explained by chance alone
